verdicts.evidence: Removing .sort() makes the 'deterministic inventory' depend on readdir order, which Node leaves unspecified. Measured on a fixture rules directory where APFS's UTF-8 byte order differs from JS code-unit order (astral-plane vs BMP filenames): readRuleSet returned slugs in a different order than pristine. On the shipped corpus this filesystem happens to return sorted order, so smoke's sortedness assertion and every other layer stayed green.

verdicts.evidence: Removing the .md filter turns every file in the rules directory into a rule. On a mission with a vendored org corpus (ADR-0057 puts corpus.json inside runward/rules/), rules --json reported count 65 with a phantom rule {slug: 'corpus.json', impact: '', title: 'corpus.json'}; a NOTES.txt became a rule the same way. No layer went red.

verdicts.evidence: /\.md$/ -> /\.md/ strips the FIRST '.md' rather than the extension. Measured on readRuleSet over a fixture directory: a file 'openapi.mdx.md' produced slug 'openapix.md' instead of 'openapi.mdx', so the slug the machine surface and explain key on is mangled. No layer went red.
